phases.name: Foundations
phases.summary: Measurement rig, memory & CPU fundamentals, modern C++, ~90 algorithm problems, both forks sampled.

phases.name: Build
phases.summary: Coming next: the flagship project or open-source work.

phases.summary: Harder algorithms, domain prep, mocks, publish.

weeks.goal: A quiet, repeatable benchmarking setup and a known noise floor.
Measured L1/L2/L3/DRAM latencies and bandwidth on your own machine.
Prove false sharing and data-layout effects with your own numbers.
Understand and measure branch misprediction; read perf record output fluently.
Know what a syscall, a TLB miss and an allocation cost — measured, not quoted.
Taste low-latency trading: a correct toy order book. Notice how much you enjoy it.
Taste GPU work: naive vs tiled matmul vs cuBLAS. Compare enjoyment with week A.
A correct, measured SPSC ring buffer — useful in both forks.
Read compiler output; know when auto-vectorisation works and when to hand-roll.
Top-down analysis on your own code, and a first fix driven by measurement.
Keep the habit alive; rest properly.
Spaced repetition on everything you missed; publish writeup #1.
~90 problems, a full numbers table, one published writeup, a leaning between the forks.
